editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. Nothing drifts or is invented: the three pre-flight checks, the TEM-vs-PEC "fewer shots" claim and the Premium/Flex caveats all match the English. A few passages are calqued from English. "desempenho de nível utilitário" misreads IBM's "utility-grade" (quantum utility), "conhecimento de fundo em ciência da informação quântica" is a literal "background knowledge", "funções contribuídas por" and "Estamos animados em lançar" read as translationese. A native editor would smooth these, but none would mislead a learner.

examples.source: to make utility-grade performance accessible out of the box

examples.suggested: para tornar acessível, de imediato, um desempenho em escala de utilidade quântica

examples.source: may not have the background quantum information science knowledge

examples.suggested: podem não ter formação em ciência da informação quântica

examples.source: functions contributed by our partners
examples.translation: funções contribuídas por nossos parceiros
examples.suggested: funções fornecidas por nossos parceiros
examples.why: 'contribuir' is intransitive in natural Portuguese, so the passive 'contribuídas por' is a calque.

examples.source: We're excited to roll out two new functions
examples.translation: Estamos animados em lançar duas novas funções
examples.suggested: Temos o prazer de lançar duas novas funções

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing would mislead a learner. That includes the precedence rule in [14], the copy semantics in [16] and the 10800 s / 3 h default in [37]. Two wording slips remain. First, the table label "**Choices**" is rendered "**Opções**" in [27], [30], [36] and [43], on a page where "opções" already means the Executor's options, so it reads as "Options: DEBUG, INFO…". Second, "Review the … API documentation" in [51] is calqued as "Revise a documentação", but in Portuguese "revisar" means to proofread or edit, so "Consulte a documentação" is the natural wording.

editor_note: Entry 67 keeps the meaning. All three break-even cases are intact: below the point the code helps, at the point the probabilities are equal, and beyond it the code is *aumentando* the logical-error chance. "absolutely not" is kept as "de forma alguma", and the term ponto de equilíbrio matches entries 65 and 68. The one defect is the calque "estaríamos apenas perdendo tempo junto com 8 qubits". It reads stiffly, and it can be taken to mean that the qubits are also losing time. A native editor would say that we waste time and 8 extra qubits.

examples.source: so we're just wasting our time along with 8 qubits if we use the code

examples.suggested: então, se usássemos o código, estaríamos apenas desperdiçando tempo e mais 8 qubits
examples.why: "junto com" copies "along with" word for word. In Portuguese it can read as the 8 qubits also losing time, when the point is that the 8 extra qubits are wasted. The meaning survives, but the phrasing is awkward.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the fault-tolerance caveats in [44], [47] and [50], so nothing here would mislead a learner. The main problem is that "noisy hardware" is calqued as "hardware barulhento" three times. Portuguese quantum literature uses "ruidoso" for noise-affected hardware ("barulhento" means acoustically loud). Two smaller things: "seamless execution" became "execução contínua" ("continuous execution"), which shifts the sense, and the course title "Basics of quantum information" is rendered with the awkward nominalized "Básicos de".

examples.source: This means the algorithm does not scale well on today's noisy hardware.
examples.translation: Isso significa que o algoritmo não escala bem no hardware barulhento atual.
examples.suggested: Isso significa que o algoritmo não escala bem no hardware ruidoso atual.
examples.why: 'Barulhento' means acoustically loud. The conventional term for quantum noise is 'ruidoso', and the same calque recurs in [47] and [50].

examples.source: The runtime `Sampler` primitive allows seamless execution of Grover circuits.
examples.translation: A primitiva `Sampler` do runtime permite a execução contínua de circuitos de Grover.
examples.suggested: A primitiva `Sampler` do runtime permite executar circuitos de Grover de forma simples e integrada.
examples.why: 'Contínua' means continuous or uninterrupted, not 'seamless' (frictionless).

examples.source: Basics of quantum information
examples.translation: Básicos de informação quântica
examples.suggested: Noções básicas de informação quântica
examples.why: 'Básicos' used as a noun is a calque. 'Noções básicas' or 'Fundamentos' is the natural rendering.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and none of it would mislead a learner. The background on the dielectric approximation, the caveat about implicit versus explicit solvent models and the CASCI comparison all match the English. The problems are consistency. "Sample-based quantum diagonalization" is rendered two ways: "baseada em amostragem" in [9], [12], [16] and [20], but "baseada em amostras" in [41], [52] and [53]. The "Qiskit Function template" appears three ways: "modelo de Função Qiskit" in [18], "template de Function do Qiskit" in [30] and "modelo de Qiskit Function" in [54]. Using "modelo" for "template" also clashes with "modelo de solvente implícito" in the same sentence in [54], so the reader cannot tell which "modelo" is meant.

examples.source: Sample-based quantum diagonalization of a chemistry Hamiltonian
examples.translation: Diagonalização quântica baseada em amostras de um Hamiltoniano químico
examples.suggested: Diagonalização quântica baseada em amostragem de um Hamiltoniano químico
examples.why: Entries [9], [12] and [16] use 'baseada em amostragem', so the SQD name should match. [52] and [53] have the same problem.

examples.source: Deploy and run a template for electronic structure simulation with an implicit solvent model
examples.translation: Implante e execute um modelo para simulação de estrutura eletrônica com um modelo de solvente implícito
examples.suggested: Implante e execute um template para simulação de estrutura eletrônica com um modelo de solvente implícito
examples.why: 'modelo' is used for both 'template' and 'model' in one sentence, which makes it ambiguous. The page also renders 'template' inconsistently: 'modelo' in [18] and [54], 'template' in [30].

examples.source: SQD IEF-PCM Qiskit Function template guide
examples.translation: guia de template de Function do Qiskit SQD IEF-PCM
examples.suggested: guia do template de Qiskit Function SQD IEF-PCM
examples.why: This conflicts with 'modelo de Função Qiskit' in [18]. Pick one rendering of the product name and use it everywhere.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the harder passages: the variational-bound and nesting logic ([22], [82], [108]), the M_J product-stage argument ([31], [177]) and the exact angle versus first-order angle argument ([171]). Nothing would mislead a learner. The method name is split: "pooled SQD" is kept in English in [22]/[26]/[31]/[72]/[83] and becomes "SQD agrupado" in [158]/[171]/[172]/[174]. There are also a few grammar slips and calques: "algumas poucas milhares" ([31], [64]; [168] correctly has "alguns milhares"), "meio-registradoras" (the text uses the masculine "registrador" everywhere else), "combinatorial" for "combinatório", "a melhor proxy" and "A twirling". The title "baseada em amostragem agrupada" ([1]) attaches "pooled" to the sampling rather than to the diagonalization.

examples.source: The published pooled SQD workflow diagonalizes several independent subsamples
examples.translation: O fluxo de trabalho de SQD agrupado publicado diagonaliza várias subamostras
examples.suggested: O fluxo de trabalho publicado do pooled SQD diagonaliza várias subamostras
examples.why: [22]/[26]/[31]/[83] keep 'pooled SQD' in English, but [158]/[171]/[172]/[174] switch to 'SQD agrupado'. The file should use one name for the method.

examples.source: (a few thousand at most)
examples.translation: (algumas poucas milhares no máximo)
examples.suggested: (no máximo alguns milhares)
examples.why: 'Milhar' is masculine. [31] has the same error ('algumas poucas milhares de bitstrings'), while [168] gets it right.

examples.source: The two half-register nucleon numbers are Hamming weights
examples.translation: Os números de núcleons das duas meio-registradoras são pesos de Hamming
examples.suggested: Os números de núcleons das duas metades do registrador são pesos de Hamming
examples.why: 'Meio-registradoras' is an awkward coined feminine form; everywhere else the register is the masculine 'registrador'. The same form appears again in [83].

examples.source: Its computational cost is combinatorial
examples.translation: Seu custo computacional é combinatorial
examples.suggested: Seu custo computacional é combinatório
examples.why: 'Combinatorial' is an anglicism; the standard Portuguese adjective is 'combinatório'.

examples.source: Pooled sample-based quantum diagonalization of a nuclear Hamiltonian
examples.translation: Diagonalização quântica baseada em amostragem agrupada de um Hamiltoniano nuclear
examples.suggested: Diagonalização quântica agrupada baseada em amostragem de um Hamiltoniano nuclear
examples.why: As written, 'agrupada' attaches to 'amostragem', so the reader takes it as 'pooled sampling'. In the English, 'pooled' qualifies the diagonalization method.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The Open Plan caveat in [27], the COBYLA noise explanation in [51] and the unweighted versus weighted Hamiltonian discussion in [22] all carry over intact. There are two expanded-acronym calques. QAOA is rendered as "Algoritmo de Otimização Aproximada Quântica" in [1], [7] and [14], which calques the English word order and makes "quântica" read as modifying "aproximada". The conventional Portuguese form is "Algoritmo Quântico de Otimização Aproximada". QUBO in [20] is "Otimização Binária Irrestrita Quadrática", where "Otimização Binária Quadrática Irrestrita" is the more natural order.

examples.source: Quantum approximate optimization algorithm
examples.translation: Algoritmo de otimização aproximada quântica
examples.suggested: Algoritmo quântico de otimização aproximada
examples.why: Following the English word order puts 'quântica' after 'aproximada', where it reads as modifying the approximation rather than the algorithm. The usual Portuguese name is 'Algoritmo Quântico de Otimização Aproximada'. The same fix applies in [7] and [14].

examples.source: Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO)
examples.translation: Otimização Binária Irrestrita Quadrática (QUBO)
examples.suggested: Otimização Binária Quadrática Irrestrita (QUBO)
examples.why: The adjectives are in an unnatural order. The standard Portuguese expansion is 'Otimização Binária Quadrática Irrestrita'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The methodology caveats in [28], [79], [85], [87] and [88], the above/below direction of the comparisons and the echo medians (56/53/142 µs) all match the English. The problems are consistency. "drift" is translated as "deriva" in [9], [16] and [28] but kept as the English "drift" in [76], [77], [88] and [92]. "randomized benchmarking" is "benchmarking randomizado" in [7] and [21] but "benchmarking aleatorizado" in [51] and [52]. "gate" switches gender ("gates nativos" in [32], "gates nativas" in [57]). "reported" is "relatadas" in the early entries and "informadas" from [68] on, and "layer fidelity" appears as both "fidelidade de camada" and "fidelidade em camadas". There is also one European-Portuguese form, "desfasam" in [44], where Brazilian usage is "defasam".

examples.source: not every gap between the two curves means the device has drifted
examples.translation: nem toda diferença entre as duas curvas significa que o dispositivo sofreu drift
examples.suggested: nem toda diferença entre as duas curvas significa que o dispositivo sofreu deriva
examples.why: Entries [9], [16] and [28] use 'deriva', but [76], [77], [88] and [92] switch to the English 'drift'. The file should pick one.

examples.source: isolated single-qubit randomized benchmarking
examples.translation: benchmarking aleatorizado de qubit único isolado
examples.suggested: benchmarking randomizado isolado de um qubit
examples.why: Entries [7] and [21] use 'benchmarking randomizado', so this is inconsistent. Placing 'isolado' after 'qubit único' also makes it read as describing the qubit rather than the benchmark.

examples.source: directly in the device's native gates
examples.translation: diretamente nas gates nativas do dispositivo
examples.suggested: diretamente nos gates nativos do dispositivo
examples.why: 'gate' is masculine in [21] and [32] ('gates nativos') but feminine here and in [44], [66], [70] and [79]. Pick one gender.

examples.source: how quickly its qubits relax and dephase
examples.translation: com que rapidez seus qubits relaxam e desfasam
examples.suggested: com que rapidez seus qubits relaxam e perdem a coerência de fase (defasam)
examples.why: 'desfasar' is the European Portuguese form. The rest of the file follows Brazilian usage, where the verb is 'defasar'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the caveats about the J normalization (factor of 2), the 0.65/0.7 fidelity figures and the two-layer fidelity "not a regression" point, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Terminology is correct and consistent (estado fundamental, função de Green retardada, dimensão de vínculo, fator de estrutura dinâmica, ansätze). A native editor would still fix a few spots. "fractionalized spinon excitations" became "excitações de spinon fracionárias" where physicists say "fracionalizadas". "trade off accuracy against computational cost" became "trocamos precisão por custo computacional", which reads as a one-way exchange. "Para equilibrar a expressividade contra a profundidade" is a calque of "balance X against Y".

examples.source: dominated by fractionalized spinon excitations
examples.translation: dominado por excitações de spinon fracionárias
examples.suggested: dominado por excitações fracionalizadas de spinons
examples.why: 'Fracionalizadas' is the standard term for fractionalization in condensed matter. 'Fracionárias' only means 'fractional'.

examples.source: we trade off accuracy against computational cost
examples.translation: trocamos precisão por custo computacional
examples.suggested: equilibramos precisão e custo computacional
examples.why: In Portuguese 'trocar X por Y' means giving up X to get Y. The English describes a balance between the two, not a one-way exchange.

examples.source: To balance expressibility against circuit depth
examples.translation: Para equilibrar a expressividade contra a profundidade do circuito
examples.suggested: Para equilibrar expressividade e profundidade do circuito
examples.why: 'Equilibrar ... contra' copies the English 'balance against'. Portuguese uses 'equilibrar X e Y'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Caveats come through intact, including "não garante necessariamente" in [62], "não indicam 'vantagem quântica' imediata" in [67] and "sem crescimento linear" in [67]. "Baseline" is rendered two ways: "linha de base" in [6], [39], [46] and [50], but "baseline" from [65] onward. "Features" is also split: "características" in [32] and "features" in [68]. [69] uses "se compostem" for "compound", which is not a real Portuguese form; it should be "se acumulem" or "se somem". The calque "quântico-aprimorada" appears in [1] and [27], and [8] has an indicative "que generaliza" where the subjunctive "generalize" is needed.

examples.source: these scaling advantages are expected to compound
examples.translation: espera-se que essas vantagens de escalonamento se compostem
examples.suggested: espera-se que essas vantagens de escalonamento se acumulem
examples.why: 'compostem' is not a valid conjugation. It is a calque of 'compound', and the natural verb here is 'acumular-se'.

examples.source: The classical AdaBoost baseline provides a compact and stable reference
examples.translation: A baseline clássica do AdaBoost fornece uma referência compacta e estável
examples.suggested: A linha de base clássica do AdaBoost fornece uma referência compacta e estável
examples.why: Entries [6], [39], [46] and [50] use 'linha de base', but from [65] on the file switches to 'baseline'. The term is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: Hybrid quantum-enhanced ensemble classification
examples.translation: Classificação ensemble híbrida quântico-aprimorada
examples.suggested: Classificação híbrida por ensemble aprimorada por computação quântica
examples.why: 'quântico-aprimorada' is a stiff calque of 'quantum-enhanced'. It also reappears as 'modelo quântico-aprimorado' in [27].

examples.source: a compact, diverse subset that generalizes better
examples.translation: um subconjunto compacto e diverso que generaliza melhor
examples.suggested: um subconjunto compacto e diverso que generalize melhor
examples.why: This describes a hypothetical subset the search is trying to find, so Portuguese requires the subjunctive.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the p=1 ~49% limit, the ε-regularization caveat and the contrast between the convergence plot and the sampled bitstring. A native editor would still change a few things. The title [1] drops the named technique: "Warm-start QAOA" becomes "Iniciar o QAOA". In [48], "clipping" is rendered "corte", which clashes with "corte" (cut) in a max-cut tutorial. Several calques also remain: "Histórico" for Background, "justa" for a tight relaxation, "referência de verdade fundamental" for ground truth, and "aconteceu de ser".

examples.source: Warm-start QAOA with the Optimization Mapper Qiskit addon
examples.translation: Iniciar o QAOA com o Qiskit addon Optimization Mapper
examples.suggested: QAOA com warm-start usando o Qiskit addon Optimization Mapper
examples.why: The title loses the method's name. It now reads as 'start QAOA', not the warm-start technique the page teaches.

examples.source: After clipping, $c^* = 1$ becomes $1 - \varepsilon = 0.75$
examples.translation: Após o corte, $c^* = 1$ se torna...
examples.suggested: Após o truncamento (clipping), $c^* = 1$ se torna...
examples.why: In a max-cut tutorial, 'corte' already means the graph cut. Using it for value clipping is ambiguous.

examples.source: the QP relaxation is tight
examples.translation: a relaxação QP é justa
examples.suggested: a relaxação QP é exata (apertada)
examples.why: 'justa' is not the usual optimization term for a tight relaxation. 'exata' or 'apertada' is clearer.

examples.source: serves as a ground-truth reference
examples.translation: serve como uma referência de verdade fundamental
examples.suggested: serve como referência exata
examples.why: 'verdade fundamental' is a literal calque of 'ground truth'.

examples.source: Background
examples.translation: Histórico
examples.suggested: Contexto
examples.why: 'Histórico' means history. The section gives conceptual background, so 'Contexto' fits.

examples.source: the optimal partition happened to be the most frequently sampled outcome
examples.translation: a partição ótima aconteceu de ser o resultado amostrado com mais frequência
examples.suggested: a partição ótima por acaso foi o resultado amostrado com mais frequência
examples.why: 'aconteceu de ser' copies the English 'happened to be'. 'por acaso foi' is the natural Portuguese.

editor_note: The rewritten entry 109 is faithful: "Post-process" becomes "Pós-processamento", the usual Portuguese heading for the Qiskit-patterns step, and its {#post-process} anchor is unchanged.

Rewritten entry 128, "Então o estado quântico correspondente é:", faithfully and naturally renders "Then the corresponding quantum state is:" and fits the amplitude-encoding flow (entries 127 and 129).
